lastWeekReview.title: Rahab and the Two Spies
bullets: Before entering the good land, Joshua sent two SPIES to search out the city of Jericho.
The spies came to the house of Rahab — a woman who had not lived a good life but BELIEVED in the true God.
When the king of Jericho sent for the spies, Rahab HID them among the flax stalks on her roof.
Rahab’s house was on the city wall, so she let the spies down through her window with a ROPE.
The spies told her to tie a SCARLET thread in her window as the sign to keep her whole household safe.
Because of her FAITH, Rahab was preserved with her family and later became an ancestor of Jesus!
lastWeekReview.discussion: Rahab believed God was real and put her trust in Him and His people — even when she had a messy past. Did you trust God this week when something felt hard or scary? Share how God preserved you and your family!
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: “…For Jehovah your God, He is God in heaven above and upon earth beneath.” — Joshua 2:11

kidsContent.text: After the spies returned from Jericho, TWO MILLION people needed to cross the River Jordan to enter the good land. But there were no bridges — and the river was flowing high and deep!
So Joshua told the priests to carry the ARK of Jehovah right into the river. The ark stood for God Himself, so this meant God was going with His people into the water.
The moment the priests’ feet touched the water, the river stopped! The waters flowing down from upstream rose up in a HEAP far away, and the priests stood on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan.

They stood there holding the ark until every single person — children, older ones, and weaker ones — had crossed over. Then Joshua had twelve men take twelve STONES from the riverbed to build a memorial.
🌟 This was the very first miracle God did for Israel in the good land — a sure sign that their God is real, true, living, and active!

image.caption: The priests carry the ark across the Jordan on dry ground

kidsContent.text: Our God Is Real and Living

Many times in your life you will see things that are just IMPOSSIBLE to explain — like people saved from a disaster, or kept safe in a car accident. The dictionary even says a miracle is a surprising event that only God can do!

Sometimes the miracles are small. Once, some brothers were painting a parking lot and dark rain clouds came. But the clouds PARTED — it rained to the left and to the right, and not a drop fell on them until the job was done!
When we see things like this, there is nothing to say except: “Wow! God is REAL. He is working for us!” God can do whatever He says, no matter how impossible it seems.
🌟 Let’s be children who know our God is real, true, living, and active — and who trust Him to do great and awesome things!

lesson.practicePoint: This week, watch for the ways God shows Himself real — big or small! When you see something you can’t explain, thank Him and say, “God, You are real, living, and active!” And believe that He can do whatever He says.

memoryVerse.text: He is your praise and He is your God, who has done these great and awesome things for you, which your eyes have seen.
memoryVerse.application: Our God is not a made-up story — He is real and living! He does great and awesome things that our own eyes can see, like drying up a whole river so millions of people could walk across on dry ground. That is why He is our praise and our God!

activity.title: 🌊 Cross the Jordan — Carry the Ark

parts.text: Materials: A “river” of two blue ribbons or a strip of blue cloth on the floor, an “ark” box (a shoebox with a handle or a small chest) for two “priests” to carry, and twelve “stones” (beanbags, paper rocks, or blocks).
Setup: Lay out the blue “river” across the room. Choose two children to be the priests who carry the ark; the rest are the tribes of Israel waiting to cross.

Round 1 — The Ark Goes First: The priests carry the ark and step into the “river.” On the leader’s call, the “waters” (kids holding the ribbon) lift and pull back — the river is dry! The priests stand still in the middle.
Round 2 — Everyone Crosses: While the priests hold the ark in the middle, all the tribes walk across the dry riverbed behind them — nobody gets left behind, including the little ones!

Round 3 — Twelve Stones: Twelve children each pick up a “stone” from the riverbed and stack them into a memorial pile on the other side. Then the priests step out, and the “waters” rush back together.
📖 Connection: God stopped a whole river so His people could cross on dry ground. Our God is real, living, and active — He still does great and awesome things today!

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: The east bank of the River Jordan. The water is high and rushing. Joshua stands with the people; two young Israelites, Asa and Talia, look nervously at the river.
The children of Israel had reached the River Jordan at last. On the other side was the good land God promised them. But the river was deep, fast, and there was no bridge.
Asa, look at that water! It’s so deep and fast. How will two million of us ever get across?
I don’t know… there’s no bridge, no boats. This looks impossible!
Do not be afraid! Watch what the living God will do. Priests — lift up the ark of Jehovah and carry it into the water!
The ark stood for God Himself. So when the priests stepped in, it meant God was going right into the river with His people.
The priests carry the ark forward. The very moment their feet touch the water, the river stops flowing.
Asa — look! The water upstream is piling up in a heap! The riverbed is turning to dry ground!
It’s a miracle! The priests are standing right in the middle, and their feet are completely dry!
Now cross over, all of you — every family, every child, every older one. God is holding back the river for us!
So all the people crossed on dry ground while the priests stood holding the ark. Then Joshua chose twelve men to carry twelve stones from the middle of the river.
Set up these twelve stones as a memorial. When your children ask, ‘What do these stones mean?’ tell them how God dried up the Jordan!
The priests step out of the riverbed onto dry land. Behind them the waters of the Jordan rush back together as before.
The water came right back the second they stepped out! Our God is real — He is living and active!
Our God is real, true, living, and active — we want to be those who know Him this way!

description.text: Setup: Mark a wide “river” down the middle of the gym with two ropes or tape lines. Pick two kids to be the “priests” who carry the “ark” (a box with handles).
Rules: When the priests carry the ark to the center of the river and freeze, the leader calls “Dry ground!” — now everyone may run across the river to the far bank.
Out: If the priests drop the ark or step out early, the “waters return” and everyone still in the river must go back and start over.
Twist: Add twelve “stones” (beanbags) in the riverbed — each round, runners must grab one and stack it into a memorial pile on the far side.
📖 Connection: God stopped the river so His people could cross on dry ground. Our God is real, living, and active!
Materials: Two ropes or tape lines, an “ark” box, twelve beanbags
Setup: Split into two tribes. Place a pile of twelve “stones” (blocks or beanbags) at the far end for each tribe — that’s the middle of the “Jordan.”
Rules: One at a time, each child runs to the riverbed, grabs one stone, races back, and stacks it into their tribe’s memorial. Then the next runner goes.
Scoring: The first tribe to carry all twelve stones back AND build a standing memorial wins — but a memorial that topples must be rebuilt!
Switch: Play again with kids carrying the stones balanced carefully, like the priests holding the ark steady.
📖 Connection: The twelve stones were a memorial so Israel would always remember God’s great miracle. We remember our God is real and living!
Materials: Twenty-four blocks or beanbags, open space
Mark out a long “river” on the grass or pavement with two chalk lines or ropes. Choose two children to carry the “ark” ahead of everyone else.
Goal: The ark-bearers walk to the middle and stand still. Only then may the tribes cross the “dry riverbed” between the lines — nobody crosses ahead of the ark!
Rule: Along the way, twelve children each pick up a natural “stone” (a rock, pinecone, or stick) from the riverbed to build a memorial on the far bank.
Finish: Gather at the memorial pile and thank God that He is real, living, and active — and still does great and awesome things for us.
Materials: Chalk or two ropes, an “ark” box, twelve natural “stones”

outdoor.tip: 🌊 The lesson is knowing God: our God is real, true, living, and active. Help the kids feel the wonder of the miracle — a whole river drying up — and connect it to the big and small miracles they can watch for in their own lives.
